Criterion: Verify that redundancy is incorporated such that failure of any single sensor, connection, processor, or display unit does not result in loss of safety-critical data or display of unsafe or misleading data. Standard: Potential failure modes, required diagnostic capability, and the effects on system safety are defined and documented. Failure modes identified, including degradation/loss due to single point failures; generation of corrupt data; memory upset conditions; blank cockpits/operator stations; and processor, system, and subsystem resets, are prevented using a combination of diagnostics capability (acceptable fault detection accuracy), fault isolation, real time principles such as Rate Monotonic Scheduling (RMS) and data stream cross check. The probability of presenting Hazardously Misleading Information (HMI) to the pilot/operator is found to be consistent with the type and mission of the aircraft. Method of Compliance: Potential failure modes are verified by inspection of the FMEA. Laboratory and flight testing under worst case loaded conditions verify that no failure modes exist that result in unsafe flight conditions. Analysis shows probability of HMI is consistent with the type and mission of the aircraft. References: JSSG-2005: 3.2.1.4.1, 3.2.1.8, 4.2.1.8, 4.2.1.4.1 MIL-STD-882 SAE ARP4761 SAE ARP5580 SAE ARP4761: 4.2 FMEA, 4.4 CCA, 4.4.2 PRA, 4.4.3 CMA 14 CFR 23.1309, 23.1311, 23.1331, 25.1309, 25.1331 plus any appropriate advisory circular(s) FAA AC-27-1 and FAA AC-29-2 provide guidance on helicopter equipment, primarily in subpart "F"

Standard: Redundancy mechanisms and switching functions operate to ensure the avionics subsystem provides SCF integrity. The probability of loss or degradation of SCFs capable of resulting in a catastrophic or critical hazard should be 10-7 or less per flight hour. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Failure mode effects analysis, SCFTA, SHA, and other design information is analyzed to identify potential failure modes and ensure redundancy is incorporated with separation to support the integrity and reliability requirements. Analysis shows single point failures meet low probability, less than 10-7 , of HMI and loss or degradation of SCFs. Analysis shows failures affecting SCFs support the SCF integrity in the standard. Test.
  (1) Lab test: SIL testing and FMET verifies redundant operations for all associated failures. Testing verifies when operating in any redundant degraded mode that any degradation status is clear to the crewmember.
  (2) Ground test: Air vehicle ground tests validate redundancy and lab test results through select test cases. Any other ground test failures impacting redundancy show the redundancy mechanization does not result in catastrophic or critical consequences. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (3) Flight test: Record any critical failures encountered related to redundancy of the avionics system. Noted failures demonstrate that any single failure does not result in the loss or degradation of SCFs.
